/*
# SimpleLayout — stack children along an axis

The stacking idiom: siblings placed one after another along
`axis`, in child order, `spacing` apart (negative overlaps). The cross axis
and all sizes stay the children's own — a child centers itself across a row
with the ordinary `y = center`. Invisible children are skipped and their
space reclaimed; a skipped child still gets the slot it would occupy, so
re-showing it needs no special case. A `Spacer` child flexes to absorb the
run's slack along the axis (between two groups it pushes them apart; one on
each side centers the run).

Written in Declare over the Layout kernel: the whole strategy is this one
pure place() — one box per laid child, aligned by index.

```declare
col: View [ x = 20, y = 20,
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 8 ],
    View [ width = 160, height = 24, cornerRadius = 6, fill = steelblue ],
    View [ width = 120, height = 24, cornerRadius = 6, fill = cadetblue ],
    View [ width = 190, height = 24, cornerRadius = 6, fill = slategray ]
    ]
```

## axis
Which way children stack: `y` (the default) or `x`. **A bare literal, not a string** —
`axis = x`, and note that `x` here is the axis token, not the position attribute.

## spacing
The gap between adjacent children. **Negative overlaps them**, which is how a stack of
cards or avatars is built.

## place()
The whole strategy: one box per laid child, positioned along the axis in child order.
**The cross axis and every size stay the children's own** — a child centres itself
across a row with the ordinary `y = center`. Override it in a subclass for custom
geometry; a `Layout`'s `place()` **may** aggregate over children, which is the one place
that is allowed.
*/

class SimpleLayout extends Layout [
    axis: Axis = y,
    spacing: number = 0,

    place() {
        const axis = this.axis
        const size = axis == "x" ? "width" : "height"
        const kids = this.laid()
        const flexing = (c) => (c).flexes === true

        // slack, only when someone flexes: the view's extent along the axis
        // minus the rigid content and the gaps between visible children
        let each = 0
        let flexN = 0
        for (const c of kids) if (c.visible && flexing(c)) flexN = flexN + 1
        if (flexN > 0) {
            let content = 0
            let visN = 0
            for (const c of kids) {
                if (!c.visible) continue
                visN = visN + 1
                if (!flexing(c)) content = content + (c)[size]
            }
            const extent = this.view == null ? 0 : (this.view)[size]
            each = Math.max(0, (extent - content - this.spacing * Math.max(0, visN - 1)) / flexN)
        }

        let pos = 0
        return kids.map((c) => {
            const flex = c.visible && flexing(c)
            const box = (axis == "x" ? ({ x: pos }) : ({ y: pos }))
            if (flex) box[axis == "x" ? "w" : "h"] = each
            if (c.visible) pos = pos + (flex ? each : (c)[size]) + this.spacing
            return box
            })
        }
    ]

/*
# Icon — the drawn mark

A small monochrome mark, **drawn** rather than typed. Fonts are not UI objects:
their glyphs are not guaranteed to be present, they rasterize differently on
every platform, and the ones that exist are the wrong shapes — a `✓` sits on the
text baseline and reads like a square-root sign, not like a checkmark. The house
already knew this in three places before it had a name for it (`Checkbox.mark`,
`Menu.check`, `Combobox.disc` are all drawn); this is that decision, stated once.

### Writing one

Subclass and override `draw`. Author the shape in a **16×16 box** — `unit`
converts it to whatever size the host asked for:

```declare-fragment
class SparkIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(unit, unit)
        d.strokeStyle = ink; d.lineWidth = weight / unit
        d.beginPath(); d.moveTo(8, 1); d.lineTo(8, 15); d.stroke()
        }
    ]
```

Overriding a **method** is the refinement path that works — re-opening an
inherited child is not (`cap:` on a `Button` subclass fails at instantiate), so
the shape lives in `draw` and everything adjustable is a slot.

### Size changes the drawing, not the shape

Every icon is ONE path. There are no per-size variants, no thresholds, nothing
redrawn at a breakpoint: `unit` scales the 16-box to whatever the host asked for,
so a 64px icon is the 16px icon at 4×, exactly.

The **stroke** is the deliberate exception. `d.lineWidth = weight / unit` sits
*inside* `d.scale(unit, unit)`, so the two cancel and the line lands at a constant
`weight` in **device pixels at every size**. An icon's line therefore matches the
1px rules and text weights it sits among, instead of fattening as it grows.

The cost is that the stroke-to-size ratio falls: 1.6px is 10% of a 16px icon, 5%
at 32, 2.5% at 64. Across 14–18px, which is every site in this corpus, that is
invisible. Past ~32 an icon starts reading as a fine-line drawing rather than a
mark — so **this set is built for chrome sizes**, and a large display icon (an
empty-state mark, an about-box graphic) would want the opposite: `d.lineWidth =
weight` *outside* the scale, so the line grows with the drawing. Real icon
systems take a third road and redraw per optical size range; that is a bigger
undertaking than this set needs.

`test/probe/iconbook.declare` shows the ramp — the same chevron and bulb at 16,
24, 32, 48 and 64 — if the tradeoff ever needs re-judging.

### What is NOT an Icon

Application art. The desktop's dock icons are the case to look at before
reaching for this class: they rest at 56px and grow under the magnification
swell, they are polychrome (`gradient(hue1, hue2)` behind a hue-parameterised
drawing), and their **width animates every frame**. Each of those alone rules
them out — the constant stroke that suits a 16px mark is 2.9% of a 56px one and
reads spindly; `ink` is a single colour; and an animated width is the one thing
this set forbids.

The line is not "drawn versus not drawn" — dock art is drawn too. It is
**chrome vocabulary versus identity**. A mark that says *close*, *expand*,
*checked*, *this is the dark theme* belongs here, at a size the host states.
A mark that says *this is Calendar* does not, and belongs to the app that owns
the identity.

Desktop has both, which is what makes it the clarifying example: its menu rows
take `WindowIcon` and `CodeIcon` from this set, while its dock keeps `DockIcon`.

### Two rules

**Scale inside the body, never with the View's `scale`.** A recording rasterizes
into a canvas sized to its own ink bounds at device resolution
(`dom-backend.ts` `rasterize()`), while `scale` is a CSS transform applied
*after* — so `scale = { width / 16 }` would rasterize 16 pixels and stretch them.
Crisp at exactly 16, soft at every other size, which is most of them. Scaling
inside the recording allocates the raster at true size instead.

**Never animate an icon's `width`.** Reading size inside `draw` makes the
recording size-dependent: an animated size re-records AND reallocates the backing
canvas every frame, which is what dragged the dock's magnification from 60 to
~25fps (`adaptive-draw-cache.md`). A static size re-records once and costs
nothing after. Measured: 120 icons re-recording their *content* every frame runs
frame-bound at 16.6ms, cheaper than the 120 text glyphs they replace.

Colour is not a rule — `ink` follows the prevailing text colour, so an icon beside
a muted label goes muted on its own, and a host that needs a different ink (a
menu row's check inverting on the hot row) simply sets it.

## ink
The mark's colour. Follows the **prevailing `textColor`**, so an icon beside a muted
label goes muted on its own. **The trap: that slot falls back to black platform-wide**,
so an icon in a context that never states a text colour renders black and vanishes on a
dark surface. State `ink` unless you know the context sets one — `IconHost` does it for
every icon built by name.

## weight
Stroke width in **final device pixels, not authored ones**. Divide by `unit` inside
`draw` (`d.lineWidth = weight / unit`) and the scale cancels, so the line lands at a
constant weight at every size and matches the 1px rules and text it sits among.

## unit
The 16-box-to-host-size scale factor. **Multiply the path by it; divide the stroke by
it.** Every icon is one path at one size, scaled — there are no per-size variants.

## isIcon
**Internal.** The marker a layout keys on to place an icon without knowing which shape
it is — not API.
*/

/*
# IconHost — a named icon, materialized

   A control names its icon (`iconLeft = TrashIcon`) rather than nesting one,
   because a control is a leaf and everything else about it is an attribute — and
   because an attribute is the one form where AUTHORED and BOUND are the same
   mechanism. `IconHost` is what turns that name into a live view, through the
   same `app.createView` seam the menu's `iconKind` already uses.

   It reserves no space when empty, so a control's `contentWidth` measures only
   the slots that are actually filled and an icon-less button needs no special
   case.

   LIMITATION, deliberate for now: the name is consumed once, at construction.
   A control whose icon must CHANGE at runtime (a play/pause toggle) is not
   served by this yet — that needs a name-valued slot the runtime re-materializes
   on change, which is a runtime feature, not a library one. Every site in this
   corpus names its icon statically.

## kind
The icon **class name** to build (`"TrashIcon"`). `""` builds nothing and the host
collapses to zero width, so an icon-less control needs no special case. **Consumed once,
at construction** — assigning a new name later does not re-materialize the icon. A name
that is only ever computed needs `use [ Name ]` to survive the build.

## ink
The colour handed to the icon this host builds. **`createView` cannot pass attributes,
so a prevailing slot is the only channel that reaches it** — this publishes `textColor`
for exactly that. Defaults to `theme.text` rather than the platform's inherited black,
which is what stops a host-built icon from rendering invisibly on a dark surface.

## onInit
Builds the named icon. Fires once.
*/

class IconHost extends View [
    kind: string = "",
    width  = { classroot.kind == "" ? 0 : this.iconSize },
    height = { this.iconSize },
    y = center,
    visible = { classroot.kind != "" },

    // THE INK CHANNEL. `createView` cannot pass attributes, so the only way to
    // reach the icon it builds is a PREVAILING slot — and the one `Icon.ink`
    // reads is `textColor`. Publishing it here is what lets a host state its
    // ink at all.
    //
    // The default matters more than it looks: prevailing `textColor` falls back
    // to 0x000000 platform-wide, so an icon that inherited it rendered BLACK —
    // fine on a light surface by luck, invisible on a dark one. Every
    // host-created icon in the corpus was doing that. `theme.text` is a floor
    // that is never invisible in either palette.

    ink: Color = { this.theme.text },
    textColor = { classroot.ink },

    onInit() { if (this.kind != "") this.root.createView(this.kind, this, ({ })) }
    ]


class Icon extends View [
    // The marker a layout keys on, so a control can place its icon without
    // caring which shape it is (the Segment/Segmented discipline).

    isIcon: boolean = true,

    // Size comes from the CONTEXT: `iconSize` is prevailing, so a menu states 16
    // once and every icon in every row answers. A use site may override it.

    width  = { this.iconSize },
    height = { this.width },
    y = center,

    // Follows the PREVAILING text colour, so an icon beside a muted label goes
    // muted on its own. The trap: that slot falls back to 0x000000 platform-wide,
    // so an icon in a context which never states a text colour renders BLACK and
    // disappears on a dark surface. State `ink` unless you know the context sets
    // one — `IconHost` does it for every icon built by name.

    ink: Color = { this.textColor },
    weight: number = 1.6,        // stroke width in FINAL pixels, not authored ones

    // 16-box → host size. Multiply the path by this; divide the stroke by it, so
    // the line keeps its true weight instead of scaling with the drawing.

    unit: number = { this.width / 16 }
    ]

/*
# Core icons

The marks the chrome uses everywhere: a chevron, a check, a close, plus/minus,
and the menu's help bulb. Each is authored in a 16×16 box and scaled to the
host's `iconSize` inside its recording (see `icon.declare`).

Geometry is a property of the SET, not of the site: one stroke weight, round caps
and joins throughout, one path per shape. Before this, the corpus drew a
checkmark two ways (stroke 2.5 mitered in `Checkbox`, 1.8 round in `Menu`) and a
chevron at least six, three of them inside the library. Ink stays local — a menu
row inverts its check on the hot row, a checkbox always uses `accentText`.
*/



/*
# ChevronIcon

The **disclosure** mark: a menu drops, a pane opens, a select expands. Every
disclosure in the chrome is this one class turned by its `dir`, which is what makes
them agree. For a direction that is itself the state — a sort order, a trend — reach
for `ArrowIcon` instead; the two must not look alike.

## dir
The resting orientation: `"down"` (the default), `"up"`, `"left"` or `"right"`. Sugar
over `angle`.

## angle
The rotation in radians, and **the primitive, so it can be sprung** — an `Accordion`
twisty turns in step with its pane sliding open rather than snapping between two
states. Rotation lives in the recording because there is no `rotation` View attribute.

## draw()
Renders the chevron. Override to replace the mark while keeping the class's role.
*/

class ChevronIcon extends Icon [
    dir: string = "down",                       // down | up | left | right
    angle: number = { classroot.dir == "up" ? Math.PI
                    : classroot.dir == "left" ? Math.PI / 2
                    : classroot.dir == "right" ? -Math.PI / 2 : 0 },

    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.lineJoin = "round"
        d.save()
        d.translate(8, 8)
        d.rotate(this.angle)
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(-3.5, -1.75)
        d.lineTo(0, 1.75)
        d.lineTo(3.5, -1.75)
        d.stroke()
        d.restore()
        }
    ]


/*
# ArrowIcon

An arrow, **not a chevron** — the two mean different things and must not look alike.
A chevron *discloses*; an arrow points at a direction that **is itself the state**:
sort ascending, a trend, a transfer. The shaft is what a chevron lacks. Tracker had
the two adjacent — a sort-direction control beside a sort-menu popper — and one shape
for both read as a mistake.

## dir
Which way it points: `"up"` (the default), `"down"`, `"left"` or `"right"`.

## angle
The rotation in radians, sprungable like `ChevronIcon`'s.

## draw()
Renders the arrow.
*/

class ArrowIcon extends Icon [
    dir: string = "up",                         // up | down | left | right
    angle: number = { classroot.dir == "down" ? Math.PI
                    : classroot.dir == "left" ? Math.PI / 2
                    : classroot.dir == "right" ? -Math.PI / 2 : 0 },

    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.lineJoin = "round"
        d.save()
        d.translate(8, 8)
        d.rotate(this.angle)
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(0, 5.2); d.lineTo(0, -5.2)     // the shaft is what a chevron lacks
        d.moveTo(-3.6, -1.6); d.lineTo(0, -5.2); d.lineTo(3.6, -1.6)
        d.stroke()
        d.restore()
        }
    ]


/*
# CheckIcon

The tick — a checked menu row, a `Checkbox`'s mark, a confirmation. **Ink stays
local**: a menu row inverts its check on the highlighted row while a checkbox always
uses the accent text colour, so the host sets `ink` rather than the icon assuming it.

## draw()
Renders the tick. Before this class the corpus drew a checkmark two ways — stroke 2.5
mitered in `Checkbox`, 1.8 round in `Menu` — which is the drift one shape ends.
*/

class CheckIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.lineJoin = "round"
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(3, 8.5)
        d.lineTo(6.5, 12)
        d.lineTo(13, 4.5)
        d.stroke()
        }
    ]


/*
# CloseIcon

The dismiss mark: a window close box, a chip's remove affordance, a dialog's corner.

## draw()
Renders the cross.
*/

class CloseIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(4.5, 4.5); d.lineTo(11.5, 11.5)
        d.moveTo(11.5, 4.5); d.lineTo(4.5, 11.5)
        d.stroke()
        }
    ]


/*
# PlusIcon

Add. Pairs with `MinusIcon` at the same stroke and cap, so a stepper's two ends match.

## draw()
Renders the plus.
*/

class PlusIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(8, 3.5); d.lineTo(8, 12.5)
        d.moveTo(3.5, 8); d.lineTo(12.5, 8)
        d.stroke()
        }
    ]


/*
# MinusIcon

Remove, and the partially-checked state of a tri-state box. Pairs with `PlusIcon`.

## draw()
Renders the bar.
*/

class MinusIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(3.5, 8); d.lineTo(12.5, 8)
        d.stroke()
        }
    ]


/*
# LightbulbIcon

The macOS Help affordance — **Apple's own `lightbulb`, ported exactly** rather than
redrawn: the outline was lifted from the live symbol at 1024pt and normalised to the
16-box.

## draw()
Renders the bulb. **This one mark is filled, and does not answer to `weight`** — an SF
Symbol is a filled contour with the stroke baked into the outline, so matching Apple
means adopting a shape, not a stroke. There is no stroke here to widen. The set's own
drawn bulb is the alternative; this is the port.
*/

// Ported EXACTLY. Not
// redrawn from a screenshot and not approximated: the outline was lifted from
// the live symbol (`NSSymbolImageRep.outlinePath` at 1024pt, 29 elements,
// bounds 1338 × 2327), normalised so the mark is 16 units tall — 9.20 wide,
// centred at x + 3.40. No y-flip: `outlinePath` already counts DOWN, like this
// canvas — flipping it stood the bulb on its head, which the overlay caught and
// a glance would not have. `test/probe/ref/render.swift` regenerates the
// reference it was measured against.
//
// It is FILLED, and that is not a lapse in a stroked set: an SF Symbol IS a
// filled contour, with the stroke baked into the outline at a chosen weight.
// Matching Apple exactly therefore means adopting a shape, not a stroke — so
// this one mark does not answer to `weight`, and cannot, because there is no
// stroke to widen. The set's own bulb is the alternative; this is the port.
//
// What the port changes, measured against the drawing it replaces: the filament
// is gone (Apple has none), the glass is a continuous teardrop rather than an
// arc with a gap, and the base is three tapering bars at 11.48 / 13.19 / 14.68
// rather than three equal rules.

class LightbulbIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.fillStyle = this.ink
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(3.4, 4.235)
        d.bezierCurveTo(3.4, 6.876, 4.982, 7.529, 5.422, 12.115)
        d.bezierCurveTo(5.449, 12.363, 5.587, 12.521, 5.848, 12.521)
        d.lineTo(10.152, 12.521)
        d.bezierCurveTo(10.42, 12.521, 10.558, 12.363, 10.585, 12.115)
        d.bezierCurveTo(11.025, 7.529, 12.6, 6.876, 12.6, 4.235)
        d.bezierCurveTo(12.6, 1.863, 10.572, 0.0, 8.0, 0.0)
        d.bezierCurveTo(5.428, 0.0, 3.4, 1.863, 3.4, 4.235)
        d.closePath()
        d.moveTo(4.438, 4.235)
        d.bezierCurveTo(4.438, 2.379, 6.068, 1.038, 8.0, 1.038)
        d.bezierCurveTo(9.932, 1.038, 11.562, 2.379, 11.562, 4.235)
        d.bezierCurveTo(11.562, 6.209, 10.255, 6.676, 9.636, 11.483)
        d.lineTo(6.37, 11.483)
        d.bezierCurveTo(5.745, 6.676, 4.438, 6.209, 4.438, 4.235)
        d.closePath()
        d.moveTo(5.827, 14.006)
        d.lineTo(10.18, 14.006)
        d.bezierCurveTo(10.407, 14.006, 10.578, 13.827, 10.578, 13.6)
        d.bezierCurveTo(10.578, 13.38, 10.407, 13.202, 10.18, 13.202)
        d.lineTo(5.827, 13.202)
        d.bezierCurveTo(5.6, 13.202, 5.422, 13.38, 5.422, 13.6)
        d.bezierCurveTo(5.422, 13.827, 5.6, 14.006, 5.827, 14.006)
        d.closePath()
        d.moveTo(8.0, 16.0)
        d.bezierCurveTo(9.066, 16.0, 9.953, 15.477, 10.021, 14.687)
        d.lineTo(5.985, 14.687)
        d.bezierCurveTo(6.034, 15.477, 6.927, 16.0, 8.0, 16.0)
        d.closePath()
        d.fill()
        }
    ]

/*
# Control

The interaction-state base every stateful control extends (docs/system-design/components-baseline.md,
Contract 3). It owns how the pointer, keyboard, and focus relate to this view — and
nothing semantic: `checked`, `value`, and their kin live on the concrete control.

The pointer half is the language's now: `hovered` and `pressed` are View's read-only
interaction intrinsics (chain-based, touch-correct, cancel-safe). What Control adds is
the CONTROL policy on top of them, as derivations every concrete control reads:

- `hot` / `down` — the styling pair: the intrinsics gated by `disabled`, with the
  keyboard-activation `flash` folded into `down`. Style against these, not the raw
  intrinsics, and a disabled control never lights up.
- `disabled` — inert: not focusable, no activation; concrete controls gate on it.
- keyboard — Space or Enter on the focused control activates it, the same `press()`
  path a pointer uses, acknowledged by flashing the pressed look.

It also owns the two things every labelled control was improvising:

- `iconLeft` / `iconRight` — decoration, by class name. A concrete control lays
  them out; Control only declares that they exist, so `Button` and `Segment`
  answer to one vocabulary.
- `menu` — the ROLE of dropping a menu. Not decoration: fifteen sites across the
  corpus call `someMenu.openFor(control)`, and the disclosure mark for that one
  role was drawn five different ways or omitted (a glyph inside the label string
  in five places, a private chevron in two, a separate `Text` in one, nothing in
  `MenuBar` and `DataGrid`). Nobody chose those differences. Setting `menu` gets
  the mark, the anchored open, the held-open styling, and Down-to-open together,
  which is the part a hand-rolled copy gets wrong one piece at a time.

Extend it to make your own control a first-class one — focusable, keyboard-activated,
and styled off the same state pair as everything the library ships:

```declare
class Stepper extends Control [ width = 90, height = 26, cornerRadius = 6,
    n: number = 0,
    fill = { down ? theme.controlPressed : hot ? theme.controlHover : theme.control },
    press() { n = n + 1 },
    onClick() { if (!disabled) press() },
    t: Text [ x = center, y = center, fontSize = 13, text = { "" + classroot.n } ]
    ]


App [ Stepper [ x = 20, y = 20 ] ]
```

## disabled
Inert: not focusable, no activation, and the gate folded into `hot`/`down` so a
disabled control never lights up. **Constrain it rather than assigning it**
(`disabled = { app.muted }`) — it is ordinary derived state. Concrete controls also
dim themselves against `theme.disabledOpacity`.

## hot
Hover under control policy — `hovered` gated by `disabled`. **Style against this, not
the raw `hovered` intrinsic**, or a disabled control lights up under the pointer. Always
false on touch, since `hovered` is.

## down
The pressed look — the `pressed` intrinsic gated by `disabled`, **with keyboard
activation folded in**, so Space/Enter flashes the same appearance a pointer press
gives. The other half of the styling pair with `hot`.

## focused
True while this control holds keyboard focus. For the *ring*, you want nothing: the
app-level `FocusRing` indicates focus for you. Read this only for a control's own
focus styling.

## focusVisible
Focused **and** the focus arrived by keyboard — the web's `:focus-visible` channel.
Cleared by blur and by a pointer press on this control, so a clicked control shows no
keyboard edge while a tabbed one does. What a `Pane` header's focus edge reads.

## iconLeft
A decorative icon for the leading slot, **named by class** (`iconLeft = "TrashIcon"`),
not nested as a child — a control is a leaf, and a name is the one form where authored
and data-bound are the same mechanism (`iconLeft = { "" + :icon }` in a replicated
toolbar). Control only declares the slot; the concrete control lays it out. A
**computed** name needs `use [ Name ]` to survive the build, since no static reference
reaches it.

## iconRight
The trailing icon slot, same vocabulary as `iconLeft`. Setting it **wins over the
chevron a `menu` would imply** — see `rightIcon`.

## menu
The menu this control drops — an instance, not a name (`menu = { app.optionsMenu }`).
Setting it is a *role*, not decoration: the disclosure mark, the anchored open below
the control, the held-open fill, and ArrowDown-to-open all follow together. **Declare
one menu and point many controls at it** rather than one per opener; the menu reads
`opener` to vary its items.

## menuOpen
True while `menu` is showing *and* this control is what opened it. **Derived, never

    focusShape() { return null },

# Segmented

A row of mutually exclusive choices — the control you reach for when the options
are few, named, and worth showing all at once. Its choices are **data**, like
`Menu`'s items and `DataGrid`'s columns:

```declare-fragment
Segmented [ width = 300, value = { app.page },
    choices = { [ ({ id: "controls", label: "Controls" }),
                 ({ id: "table",    label: "Table" }),
                 ({ id: "grid",     label: "DataGrid" }) ] },
    input(v: object) { app.page = "" + v }
    ]
```

### Why data, and not `Segment` children

Because the sliding highlight cannot be built any other way. The pill has to know
which choice is selected and how wide each one is, and a constraint may not ask
the view tree that: `childViews` carries **set membership only**, so `.length` is
live while anything reaching into the collection is refused —
`aggregation over a reactive node collection … derive from data [DECLARE7001]`.
The compiler names the answer.

It is also the mainstream shape. UIKit's segments are titles in an array, SwiftUI
picks from a `ForEach`, Ant Design takes `options`; only Material and WinUI name
the item at all, and both compound it. A bare `Segment` class was the minority
pattern — and bare enough that two apps in this corpus had taken the name for a
paragraph of prose.

### Equal widths — a choice, not a limitation

Segments divide the control's width evenly. This is a DESIGN decision and it
could be otherwise: a `Layout`'s `place()` may aggregate over children — that is
how `SimpleLayout` sizes a variable-width row — so a strategy that placed each
segment by its own label and interpolated the pill between neighbours is
buildable. The `DECLARE7001` refusal binds constraints reaching into the view
tree, not the layout strategy whose job that is. Three reasons not to:

- **The systems that call this a segmented control agree.** UIKit divides evenly
  by default (`apportionsSegmentWidthByContent` is opt-in), as does SwiftUI's
  segmented `Picker`. The ones that size to content — Bootstrap, Ant — are really
  styling a row of buttons.
- **Apple's guidance makes it a content rule**: keep segment labels short and
  similar in length. Equal width enforces that rather than tolerating it. One long
  label makes the whole control look wrong, which is the feedback you want.
- **The sliding pill.** At equal widths it translates at constant width. At
  variable widths it would have to morph its width WHILE travelling, which reads
  as rubbery and worsens the more the labels differ. Most platforms never meet
  this, because their highlight pops.

The cost is real and worth stating plainly: **a `Segmented` does not self-size to
its labels.** Set `width`, or accept `segMin × choices.length`.

### The pill

The highlight springs a NORMALIZED LANE — a float index — not pixels. `x` is then
`lane × segW`, so a resize recomputes `segW` and the pill **snaps** to the right
place instead of skating across the bar on every layout change. Calendar's tab
strip discovered this; it is the one thing the bespoke copies did better than the
library, and it is now here.

The look is the library's: the chosen segment wears a raised `surface` pill with
a hairline. The motion is calendar's. Neither app was wrong about the half it got
right (`chrome-divergences.md` D9).

```declare
App [ width = 340, height = 130, page: string = "one",
    Segmented [ x = 20, y = 20, width = 300, value = { app.page },
        choices = { [ ({ id: "one", label: "One" }),
                     ({ id: "two", label: "Two" }),
                     ({ id: "three", label: "Three" }) ] },
        input(v: object) { app.page = "" + v }

    Text [ x = 20, y = 74, text = { "showing: " + app.page } ]
    ]
```

The active choice. Bind it to your own state and override `input` to own the
destination, or leave it alone and read `value` back — a `Segmented` works
standalone. Compared against each item's `choice` by identity, so any value type
works.

## isSegmented
**Internal.** The marker a `SegmentedItem` reads to recognize its parent. A
`.declare` class cannot hold a reactive cell without declaring it, so a marker is
necessarily surface — that does not make it API.

## choices
The segments, as **records**: `{ id, label }` or `{ id, icon }` — the same vocabulary

## input()
**Where the choice goes**, receiving the picked `id`. The default writes `value`;
override it to own the destination.

## pick()
Selects a choice by id, routing through `input`. The seam a segment calls.

## disabled
Disables the whole control. **A segment is not separately disable-able** — a disabled

## segMin
The per-segment width used when you set no `width` on the control. Because a
`Segmented` **does not self-size to its labels**, this is what decides the default

## count
How many choices there are, floored at 1 so the width arithmetic never divides by zero.

## segW
One segment's width — the control's width divided by the count. What the pill and every

## idx
Which choice is live, as an index into `choices`, from the **data** — the only place the

## lane
The pill's position as a **float index**, sprung toward `idx`. The whole reason the pill

## segs()
The segment views, for the keyboard rove. A handler-only walk — a constraint may not
aggregate the view tree.

## roveFrom()
Moves keyboard focus to the adjacent segment. Arrows rove; Space or Enter picks where

// difference between them is what is SUBTRACTED from the disc — nothing, half, a
// bite. The argument against: Apple's own triad is outline sun, outline crescent,

// the one of the three whose meaning IS its fill. Measured, our filled sun runs
// ×2.18 the ink of `sun.max` and our filled moon ×1.21 of `moon`, while our

How many rays surround the disc. Eight by default; lowering it reads lighter at small
sizes.

## solid
`false` (the default) draws Apple's ring; `true` fills the disc. **The ring is drawn a
touch smaller than the filled disc on purpose** — a stroke straddles its path, so an
outline at the filled radius reads as the larger mark.

## draw()
Renders the disc and its rays.

        d.fillStyle = this.ink
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        // The ring is drawn a touch smaller than the solid disc: a stroke straddles
        // its path, so an outline at the filled radius reads as the larger mark.
        d.beginPath()
        d.arc(8, 8, classroot.solid ? 3.5 : 3.15, 0, Math.PI * 2, false)
        if (classroot.solid) d.fill()
        else d.stroke()
        for (let i = 0; i < classroot.rays; i++) {
            const a = (i / classroot.rays) * Math.PI * 2
            const c = Math.cos(a), s = Math.sin(a)
            d.beginPath()
            d.moveTo(8 + c * 5.3, 8 + s * 5.3)

//

// closed path and you get Apple's, where the horns taper because the two arcs
// meet at a point. Nothing about the geometry changes — only what is done with it.

an arc pair leaves.

fills it for a solid crescent. **One path, two renditions** — nothing about the geometry
changes, only what is done with it.

# FocusRing

The traveling focus indicator — the OpenLaszlo 3.4 `focusoverlay` line, on the
reactive core, at its third form: a SHAPE-HUGGING rounded outline whose
terminus reshapes to the focused control's own silhouette (library-charter §6
— the ring springs position, size, AND cornerRadius; a Radio's row ring, a
pill Switch's ring, and a text field's ring differ because the targets do).

The layered model (charter, ratified):

- **The fact** — the ring listens to Focus (a `Focus [ onFocusChange(v: View) { … } ]` member) and
  tracks the target's root-space geometry on EVERY change, pointer or
  keyboard. A pointer focus PARKS the ring there silently (snap, no show) —
  so the next Tab's flight departs from the control the user just clicked,
  never from a stale perch.
- **Roles, theme-elected** — `theme.focusRing`: `"both"` (or `true`, the
  default) · `"travel"` (flight + the OL idle fade) · `"rest"` (no flight —
  the ring appears in place and stays) · `false` (no ring; the theme's
  components carry the at-rest indication — the invariant lives with the
  THEME+components pair). While keyboard modality holds and the role includes
  rest, the ring RESTS — no idle fade; a pointer press clears modality and
  the ring hides (web :focus-visible semantics).
- **The flight is the flourish** — `theme.focusAnimate = false` (the
  sampler's "Animate focus transitions" toggle) snaps every move; the
  underdamped travel is default-on.

It arrives automatically with any Control-descended component (the OL
`canvas.focusclass` default); declare your own `FocusRing [ ]` (or subclass)
to replace it. Pure chrome: never focusable, never a pointer target.
(v1 limits, recorded: root-space bounds are summed through the parent chain —
a scrolled container is not compensated; the silhouette is the target's
`cornerRadius` — a `focusShape()` override protocol arrives with the
emulation passes.)

**You do not instantiate this, and you do not position it.** Tab between the controls
below and watch it fly; the members exist for a subclass that replaces the rendition,
and for the theme tokens that elect its behaviour.

```declare
row: View [ x = 20, y = 20,
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 12 ],
    Button [ label = "One" ],
    Button [ label = "Two" ],
    Checkbox [ label = "Three" ]
    ]
```

## shown
Whether the ring is visible. **A pointer focus parks it silently** — geometry current,
ring hidden — so the next Tab departs from the control the user just clicked rather
than from a stale perch.

## placed
Whether the ring has ever had a target to park on. **The first appearance never flies**,
because a flight from nowhere is a streak across the app.

## ringRole()
The theme's election, from `theme.focusRing`: `"both"` (the default), `"travel"`
(flight plus the OpenLaszlo idle fade), `"rest"` (appears in place and stays, no
flight), or `"off"`. **`"off"` is legitimate only when the theme's own controls carry
an at-rest focus indication** — the invariant belongs to the theme-and-components pair,
not to the ring alone.

## restRole()
Whether the elected role includes resting — a resting ring does not idle-fade.

## travelRole()
Whether the elected role includes the flight.

## snapTo()
Lands the ring on its target immediately, skipping the flight. What a pointer focus, a
first appearance, and `theme.focusAnimate = false` all use — **and what a target moving
under a resting ring uses**, so a dragged slider thumb carries the ring rigidly instead
of springing after it.

## overlayUp
True while an overlay owns the keyboard (an open `Menu`). **The ring stands down** —
the menu's own rover is the focus story, and a page ring poking around a panel reads as
chrome fighting chrome.

## idle
True once a travel-role ring has sat still long enough to fade out — the OpenLaszlo
idle behaviour. A resting ring never sets it.

## draw()
Renders the outline: four corner arcs with arms whose length is a pure function of
distance from the target, so the physics does the choreography. Override to replace the
rendition entirely. `theme.focusSights = true` restores the open-bracket "target
sights" reading; `theme.focusRingInnerWidth` adds the Fluent two-tone band.

## tx
**Internal.** The target x the springs chase.

## ty
**Internal.** The target y.

## tw
**Internal.** The target width.

## th
**Internal.** The target height.

## trad
**Internal.** The target corner radius — the silhouette reshapes as the ring travels.

## rad
**Internal.** The ring's current corner radius, sprung toward `trad`.

## gen
**Internal.** The idle-fade generation counter, so a retarget cancels the pending fade.
*/

    // stands down while it's up — the menu's rover is the focus story, and
    // a page ring poking around a panel reads as chrome fighting chrome

    tx: number = 0,
    ty: number = 0,
    tw: number = 0,
    th: number = 0,
    trad: number = 8,
    rad: number = 8,
    shown: boolean = false,
    placed: boolean = false,                     // has the ring EVER had a target to park on?

    idle: boolean = false,

    ringRole()  { const r = this.theme.focusRing; return r == false ? "off" : r == true || r == null ? "both" : r },

    travelRole() { const r = this.ringRole(); return r == "both" || r == "travel" },

    snapTo() { this.x = this.tx; this.y = this.ty; this.width = this.tw; this.height = this.th; this.rad = this.trad },

    // tracked through the parent chain and focusShape(), so an arrow-keyed
    // slider thumb (or a reflowing layout) moves the resting ring with it.
    // The band sits OUTSIDE the silhouette: inner edge touching the control's
    // boundary (the Mac halo's hug), displaced by gap + half the stroke.

    focus: Focus [
        onGeometry(g: FocusGeometry) {
            if (g.root != this.root) return
            // TRAVEL WITH the target's scroller: the ring's surface re-hosts
            // inside the scrolled container and positions in ITS content
            // coordinates — the platform then carries ring and control
            // together, zero lag, no per-scroll re-derive (the sticky-frame
            // inverse). A backend without the ride keeps root-space reactive
            // positioning.

            const prevHome = (this)._lastHome
            const hadHome = (this)._hasHome === true
            const px = classroot.x
            const py = classroot.y
            const homed = classroot.travelWith(g.scroller)

            const gy = homed ? g.homeY : g.y
            // Crossing scroll HOMES (the bar's button → a control in the
            // scrolled page): the flight must still fly. The ring's current
            // position converts through ROOT space into the DESTINATION
            // home's coordinates — same painted spot, new numbers — and the
            // springs then travel entirely within the new space (correct
            // even if that pane scrolls mid-flight).
            if (hadHome && prevHome != g.scroller) {
                const toRoot = prevHome == null || prevHome == this.root

            // ring — a dragged slider thumb, a reflow — takes the ring with it

            // discriminator is target IDENTITY (a handler-scratch expando — not

            if (classroot.restRole()) { classroot.idle = false; return }

    // the terminus reshapes to the control it surrounds.

    Spring [ attribute = y,      to = { classroot.ty }, stiffness = 220, damping = 16 ],
    Spring [ attribute = width,  to = { classroot.tw }, stiffness = 220, damping = 18 ],
    Spring [ attribute = height, to = { classroot.th }, stiffness = 220, damping = 18 ],

    // the OL brackets and the shape-hugging outline are ONE rendition at two
    // coverages: four corner-anchored strokes whose straight arms extend
    // toward each edge's midpoint by cov ∈ (0..1]. cov = 1 → arms meet, a
    // closed outline; cov low → open corner brackets ("target sights").
    // Coverage is a pure function of DISTANCE from target, so the physics
    // does the choreography: a flight breaks the ring open mid-air and the
    // settle closes the sights around the new silhouette. Small targets skip
    // the bracket phase (a ring around a radio dot has no arms to open).

    draw(d: Draw) {
        const w = this.width, h = this.height
        const Q = Math.PI / 2
        const dist = Math.abs(this.x - this.tx) + Math.abs(this.y - this.ty) + Math.abs(this.width - this.tw) + Math.abs(this.height - this.th)
        const small = Math.min(w, h) < 40
        // Ruled 2026-07-17: the ring travels as a CLOSED outline, source shape
        // to destination shape — no bracket mode intervening. The sights
        // rendition survives behind `theme.focusSights = true` (data, not a
        // code path) for its possible return: fully open in motion, arms
        // sweeping shut inside the last 16px of settle.
        const cov = this.theme.focusSights == true && !small ? Math.max(0.22, 1 - dist / 16) : 1

        // The indicator is ONE band or TWO, by data: `focusRingInnerWidth` > 0
        // adds an inner stroke between the control and the outer one — the
        // Fluent (Redmond) two-tone focus rectangle, black over white. Both
        // passes are the same outline at different insets; the flight, the
        // sights, and the silhouette machinery are shared, not forked.
        const iw = typeof this.theme.focusRingInnerWidth == "number" ? this.theme.focusRingInnerWidth : 0
        const pass = (ins, lwp, color) => {
            const r = Math.max(1, Math.min(this.rad - ins, Math.min(w, h) / 2 - ins))
            const ax = Math.max(0, ((w - 2 * ins) / 2 - r) * cov)      // horizontal arm length

            d.lineWidth = lwp
            d.beginPath()
            // each corner: arc + arms, inset symmetrically
            d.moveTo(ins + r + ax, ins); d.lineTo(ins + r, ins); d.arc(ins + r, ins + r, r, -Q, Math.PI, true); d.lineTo(ins, ins + r + ay)

            d.moveTo(ins + r + ax, h - ins); d.lineTo(ins + r, h - ins); d.arc(ins + r, h - ins - r, r, Q, Math.PI); d.lineTo(ins, h - ins - r - ay)
            d.stroke()
            }
        pass(0, lw, typeof this.theme.focusColor == "number" ? this.theme.focusColor : this.theme.accent)

        }

    // focus edge included. (When the calendar moves onto the component library
    // this goes away and the house rendition takes over.)

    content: TextInput [ x = 13, y = 50, width = { parent.width - 26 }, height = { parent.height - 60 }, multiline = true, wrap = true,

App [ minWidth = 360, minHeight = 420, appName = "Declare Calendar",

    barNarrow: boolean = { this.root.width < 560 },        // the bar tiers to TWO ROWS: controls above, date nav below

    mode: string = "month",

    navYear: number = 0,
    navMonth: number = 0,      // month is 1-based
    navKey: string = "",

    // The visible date, derived. A sentinel rather than a literal date keeps the

    year: number = { this.root.navYear == 0 ? CAL_BOOT.getFullYear() : this.root.navYear },
    month: number = { this.root.navMonth == 0 ? CAL_BOOT.getMonth() + 1 : this.root.navMonth },
    todayKey: string = { this.root.keyOf(CAL_BOOT) },
    anchorKey: string = { this.root.navKey == "" ? this.root.todayKey : this.root.navKey },
    monthRows: number = { this.root.computeMonthRows() },
    yearSeen: boolean = false,
    selectedId: number = -1,
    openSection: number = 0,

    // drag state: the event being moved, a snapshot for the ghost, the grab offset

    dragId: number = -1,
    dragging: boolean = false,
    dropKey: string = "",
    dragTitle: string = "",
    dragCat: string = "",
    dragTimeLabel: string = "",
    dragW: number = 0,
    dragH: number = 0,
    grabDX: number = 0,
    grabDY: number = 0,
    downX: number = 0,
    downY: number = 0,

    /* The address is ENVIRONMENT-AWARE: standalone, the fixture sits beside the
       app; hosted (the desktop passes env.base — its own transport's path to
       this app's home), the same relative address resolves through that base.
       `auto` covers the hosted case, where env lands after init: the url
       CHANGES when base arrives and the source refetches the right address. */

    data: DataSource [ auto = true, url = { ("" + (this.root.env.base || "")) + "data/events.json" } ],

    /* The model is DERIVED, not built: `cal.contents` recomputes when the visible
       month or the events change, and keyed replication (`:key`, `:id`) makes each

       derivation, deferred until first visited and memoized on the year. */

    cal: Dataset [ contents = { this.root.buildModel() } ],
    yearCal: Dataset [ contents = { this.root.yearSeen ? this.root.buildMonths() : this.root.emptyYear() } ],

    // the detail panel slides in on this value; the body shrinks by the same amount

    panelInset: number = 0,
    Spring [ attribute = panelInset, to = { this.root.selectedId >= 0 ? this.root.panelW : 0 }, stiffness = 240, damping = 30 ],

    // geometry

    bodyW: number = { this.root.width - (this.root.panelOverlay ? 0 : this.root.panelInset) },   // an overlaying panel never squeezes the grid
    bodyH: number = { this.root.height - this.root.barH },
    headH: number = 30,
    miniW: number = { (this.root.bodyW - 2 * this.root.pad - this.root.gap * 3) / 4 },
    miniH: number = { (this.root.bodyH - 2 * this.root.pad - this.root.gap * 2) / 3 },
    miniCellW: number = { (this.root.miniW - 20) / 7 },
    miniRowH: number = { (this.root.miniH - 44) / 6 },

    /* The focus rectangle: (c0,r0) is where the frame starts, (nc,nr) how many
       columns/rows it spans. Month is the whole grid; week springs onto the anchor
       row, day onto the anchor cell. Only a view switch moves the four springs. */

    anchorCol: number = { this.root.gridIndexOf(this.root.anchorKey) % 7 },
    anchorRow: number = { Math.floor(this.root.gridIndexOf(this.root.anchorKey) / 7) },
    c0To: number = { this.root.mode == "day" ? this.root.anchorCol : 0 },
    r0To: number = { this.root.mode == "week" || this.root.mode == "day" ? this.root.anchorRow : 0 },
    ncTo: number = { this.root.mode == "day" ? 1 : 7 },
    nrTo: number = { this.root.mode == "week" || this.root.mode == "day" ? 1 : this.root.monthRows },
    c0: number = 0,
    r0: number = 0,
    nc: number = 7,
    nr: number = 6,
    Spring [ attribute = c0, to = { this.root.c0To }, stiffness = 150, damping = 24, mass = 0.9, epsilon = 0.002 ],
    Spring [ attribute = r0, to = { this.root.r0To }, stiffness = 150, damping = 24, mass = 0.9, epsilon = 0.002 ],
    Spring [ attribute = nc, to = { this.root.ncTo }, stiffness = 150, damping = 24, mass = 0.9, epsilon = 0.002 ],
    Spring [ attribute = nr, to = { this.root.nrTo }, stiffness = 150, damping = 24, mass = 0.9, epsilon = 0.002 ],
    colW: number = { (this.root.bodyW - 2 * this.root.pad - this.root.gutter) / this.root.nc },
    rowH: number = { (this.root.bodyH - this.root.headH) / this.root.nr },
    blockness: number = { this.root.clamp(2 - this.root.nr, 0, 1) },   // 0 = month chips, 1 = time blocks — keyed on the FOCUS SPAN

    // (one focused row IS a time view), never on pixel height: a short-landscape
    // day still resolves to blocks (rowH-keyed, it stalled at 0.27 there — chips
    // posing as a day view, with in-day rescheduling silently dead), and a tall
    // monitor's month can never start half-morphing its chips. Riding `nr`
    // keeps the morph continuous: chips hold shape while the focus zooms,
    // then resolve into blocks over the last row of travel.

    gutter: number = { this.root.blockness * 52 },                             // hour-label gutter, opens in time views

    /* Year zoom: `yearZoom` (0→1) shrinks the month surface into its slot in the 4×3 year
       grid while the other eleven months resolve around it. `yearScale` scales the
       surface and the surrounding grid in lock-step. */

    myCol: number = { (this.root.month - 1) % 4 },
    myRow: number = { Math.floor((this.root.month - 1) / 4) },
    slotX: number = { this.root.pad + this.root.myCol * (this.root.miniW + this.root.gap) },
    slotY: number = { this.root.pad + this.root.myRow * (this.root.miniH + this.root.gap) },
    yearScale: number = { this.root.lerp(this.root.bodyW / this.root.miniW, 1, this.root.yearZoom) },
    yearZoom: number = 0,
    Spring [ attribute = yearZoom, to = { this.root.mode == "year" ? 1 : 0 }, stiffness = 150, damping = 24, mass = 0.9, epsilon = 0.002 ],

    periodLabel: string = {
        this.root.mode == "year"  ? "" + this.root.year
      : this.root.mode == "month" ? this.root.monthName(this.root.month) + " " + this.root.year
      : this.root.mode == "week"  ? this.root.weekLabel(this.root.anchorKey)
      :                       this.root.dayLabel(this.root.anchorKey) },

    // ── helpers ──

    lerp(a: number, b: number, t: number) -> number { return a + (b - a) * t },
    clamp(v: number, a: number, b: number) -> number { return Math.max(a, Math.min(b, v)) },

    // blend two 0xRRGGBB colors channel-wise

    mix(a: number, b: number, t: number) -> number {
        const c = (x, y) => Math.round(x + (y - x) * t)
        return (c((a >> 16) & 255, (b >> 16) & 255) << 16) | (c((a >> 8) & 255, (b >> 8) & 255) << 8) | c(a & 255, b & 255)
        },
    monthName(m: number) -> string { return ["January","February","March","April","May","June","July","August","September","October","November","December"][m - 1] },
    dowName(i: number) -> string { return ["Sun","Mon","Tue","Wed","Thu","Fri","Sat"][i] },
    dowLong(i: number) -> string { return ["Sunday","Monday","Tuesday","Wednesday","Thursday","Friday","Saturday"][i] },
    keyOf(dt: object) -> string { return dt.getFullYear() + "-" + (dt.getMonth() + 1) + "-" + dt.getDate() },
    parseKey(k: string) -> object { const p = k.split("-").map(Number); return new Date(p[0], p[1] - 1, p[2]) },
    gridIndexOf(key: string) -> number {                       // a day's 0..41 slot in the month grid
        const first = new Date(this.year, this.month - 1, 1)
        const start = new Date(this.year, this.month - 1, 1 - first.getDay())
        const d = this.root.parseKey(key)
        return Math.round((Date.UTC(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate())
                         - Date.UTC(start.getFullYear(), start.getMonth(), start.getDate())) / 86400000)
        },
    shortTime(min: number) -> string {
        const h = Math.floor(min / 60), mm = min % 60, ap = h < 12 ? "a" : "p"
        let hh = h % 12; if (hh == 0) hh = 12
        return mm == 0 ? hh + ap : hh + ":" + (mm < 10 ? "0" + mm : "" + mm) + ap
        },
    hourLabel(h: number) -> string { const ap = h < 12 ? "AM" : "PM"; let hh = h % 12; if (hh == 0) hh = 12; return hh + " " + ap },
    weekLabel(k: string) -> string {
        const d = this.root.parseKey(k)
        const s = new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate() - d.getDay())
        const e = new Date(s.getFullYear(), s.getMonth(), s.getDate() + 6)
        return this.root.monthName(s.getMonth() + 1) + " " + s.getDate() + " – "
             + (s.getMonth() == e.getMonth() ? "" : this.root.monthName(e.getMonth() + 1) + " ") + e.getDate()
        },
    dayLabel(k: string) -> string { const d = this.root.parseKey(k); return this.root.dowLong(d.getDay()) + ", " + this.root.monthName(d.getMonth() + 1) + " " + d.getDate() },

    // -> number, not Color: these return a CONCRETE 0xRRGGBB (theme slots are
    // never null at read time), and number is what mix() blends — the
    // nullable Color return would refuse every mix(catFill(…), …) call site.
    // (Surfaced when compile-time path plans made datapath bodies typecheckable.)

    catFill(c: string) -> number { const t = this.theme; return c == "holiday" ? t.holidayBg : c == "astro" ? t.astroBg : c == "milestone" ? t.milestoneBg : t.defaultBg },
    catText(c: string) -> number { const t = this.theme; return c == "holiday" ? t.holidayText : c == "astro" ? t.astroText : c == "milestone" ? t.milestoneText : t.defaultText },

    /* ── the two palettes — every color in the app, named by role ──

       LIGHT is house San Francisco: `bg`, `line`, `text`, `textMuted`,
       `textFaint`, `accent`, `control` and `controlSelected` are the preset's own
       values, to the byte.

       DARK deliberately is not, and the reason is the grid. House dark is
       STEPPED — bg → surface → control each a visible rung apart (ΔE 5.4 and
       7.7). A month is a 2D tiling of 42 equal cells, and stepped surfaces there
       read as corduroy, so this palette is FLAT and deep instead (the same two
       gaps, ΔE 2.6 and 2.5) with one bright exception: `controlSelected` sits 4 L*
       ABOVE house so the selection still pops out of the quiet field.
       `textMuted` drops ~8 L* to hold its hierarchy against the flatter
       surfaces. `text` and `accent` are house exactly, in both modes.

       This is the corpus's only 2D-tiled surface — the tracker is a list, with
       rules between its rows, and runs house dark untouched. So this stays an
       app palette rather than a second preset: one example is not a pattern. */

    darkTheme() { return ({
        bg: 0x0D151E, surface: 0x101A24, cellBg: 0x18242F, outOfMonthBg: 0x101922, weekendBg: 0x141F2A,
        todayBg: 0x14304F, dropTargetBg: 0x1E3C5E, dropTargetRing: 0x6BA4F0, line: 0x22323E, gridLine: 0x1B2934,
        text: 0xE7EEF2, textMuted: 0x8A9BA6, textFaint: 0x54626E, dayNumber: 0xC7D3DC, bodyText: 0xB4C2CC,
        hourLabel: 0x53636F,
        accent: 0x4C8DFF, accentSecondary: 0x37E0C8, currentDayText: 0x9CC4FF, todayText: 0x7FB0FF,
        control: 0x131F29, controlSelected: 0x244463,
        fieldBg: 0x0F1A25, fieldEdge: 0x2A3B49,
        sectionBg: 0x16222E, sectionOpenBg: 0x1B2B3B,
        miniBg: 0x121C26, miniCurrentBg: 0x14283F, miniDayText: 0x9FB0BB, miniDayFaint: 0x33414C,
        holidayBg: 0x14321F, holidayText: 0x74D89B, astroBg: 0x241F3D, astroText: 0xB6A6F0,
        milestoneBg: 0x33280F, milestoneText: 0xF0C36B, defaultBg: 0x123050, defaultText: 0x8FB6F0 }) },
    lightTheme() { return ({
        bg: 0xF4F6FA, surface: 0xFFFFFF, cellBg: 0xFFFFFF, outOfMonthBg: 0xEDF0F5, weekendBg: 0xF1F4F8,
        todayBg: 0xDCE9FF, dropTargetBg: 0xC7DDFF, dropTargetRing: 0x2E6FE0, line: 0xDBE1E9, gridLine: 0xE4E9EF,
        text: 0x1B2733, textMuted: 0x6C7A88, textFaint: 0xAAB4BE, dayNumber: 0x2A3542, bodyText: 0x3E4C59,
        hourLabel: 0x99A5B0,
        accent: 0x2E6FE0, accentSecondary: 0x12A594, currentDayText: 0x2E6FE0, todayText: 0x2E6FE0,
        control: 0xE7EBF1, controlSelected: 0xD3E2FC,
        fieldBg: 0xFFFFFF, fieldEdge: 0xDBE1E9,
        sectionBg: 0xF1F5F9, sectionOpenBg: 0xE6EEF8,
        miniBg: 0xFFFFFF, miniCurrentBg: 0xE7F0FF, miniDayText: 0x3E4C59, miniDayFaint: 0xBFC8D2,
        holidayBg: 0xDCF3E4, holidayText: 0x1E7A44, astroBg: 0xEBE6FB, astroText: 0x5B3FB8,
        milestoneBg: 0xFBEFD6, milestoneText: 0x9A6A11, defaultBg: 0xDCE8FE, defaultText: 0x2456B0 }) },
    eventsOn(all: array, y: number, m: number, d: number) -> array {
        return all.filter(e => e.y == y && e.m == m && e.d == d).sort((a, b) => a.start - b.start || a.id - b.id)
                  .map((e, i) => Object.assign({}, e, { timeLabel: this.root.shortTime(e.start), idx: i, dur: e.end - e.start }))
        },
    computeMonthRows() {
        const first = new Date(this.year, this.month - 1, 1)
        return Math.ceil((first.getDay() + new Date(this.year, this.month, 0).getDate()) / 7)
        },

    /* ## The model
       `buildModel` builds the visible month's grid, each day carrying a copy of its
       events tagged with its grid row (so only the focused row morphs to blocks).
       `buildMonths` builds the year's twelve minis; its only tracked input is the
       year, so it rebuilds once a year and never on a view switch. */

    buildModel() {
        const all = this.root.data.read(["events"]) ?? []
        const cols = [0,1,2,3,4,5,6].map(i => ({ name: this.root.dowName(i), col: i }))
        const hours = Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, h) => ({ h: h, label: this.root.hourLabel(h) }))
        const first = new Date(this.year, this.month - 1, 1)
        const start = new Date(this.year, this.month - 1, 1 - first.getDay())
        const rows = this.root.computeMonthRows()
        const grid = []
        for (let i = 0; i < rows * 7; i++) {
            const dt = new Date(start.getFullYear(), start.getMonth(), start.getDate() + i)
            const row = Math.floor(i / 7)
            grid.push({ key: this.root.keyOf(dt), num: dt.getDate(), dow: this.root.dowName(dt.getDay()), col: i % 7, row: row,
                        inMonth: dt.getMonth() == this.month - 1, weekend: dt.getDay() == 0 || dt.getDay() == 6,
                        today: this.root.keyOf(dt) == this.todayKey, current: this.root.keyOf(dt) == this.anchorKey,
                        events: this.root.eventsOn(all, dt.getFullYear(), dt.getMonth() + 1, dt.getDate()).map(e => Object.assign({}, e, { dayRow: row })) })
            }
        return { grid: grid, cols: cols, hours: hours }
        },
    buildMonths() {
        const all = this.root.data.value != null ? this.root.data.value.events : []
        const months = []
        for (let m = 1; m <= 12; m++) {
            const st = new Date(this.year, m - 1, 1 - new Date(this.year, m - 1, 1).getDay())
            const cells = []
            for (let i = 0; i < 42; i++) {
                const dt = new Date(st.getFullYear(), st.getMonth(), st.getDate() + i)
                cells.push({ num: dt.getDate(), col: i % 7, row: Math.floor(i / 7), inMonth: dt.getMonth() == m - 1,
                             today: this.root.keyOf(dt) == this.todayKey,
                             has: dt.getMonth() == m - 1 && all.some(e => e.y == dt.getFullYear() && e.m == m && e.d == dt.getDate()) })
                }
            months.push({ m: m, name: this.root.monthName(m), mcol: (m - 1) % 4, mrow: Math.floor((m - 1) / 4), cells: cells })
            }
        return { months: months }
        },
    emptyYear() { return { months: [] } },

    /* ## Navigation
       A view switch is just a new `mode` (the focus rect springs); a page turn is
       a new navYear/navMonth/navKey. The model derives from those, so navigation
       only sets state — and `today()` is a return to the defaults. */

    goMode(m: string) { this.selectedId = -1; this.mode = m; if (m == "year") this.yearSeen = true },
    pickDay(key: string) {
        const d = this.root.parseKey(key)
        this.navKey = key; this.navYear = d.getFullYear(); this.navMonth = d.getMonth() + 1; this.selectedId = -1; this.mode = "day"
        },
    pickMonth(m: number) { this.navMonth = m; this.selectedId = -1; this.mode = "month" },
    today()       { this.navYear = 0; this.navMonth = 0; this.navKey = "" },
    step(dir: number) {
        const a = this.root.parseKey(this.anchorKey)      // paging keeps the anchor day coherent
        if (this.mode == "year") {
            const y = this.year + dir
            this.navYear = y
            this.navKey = y + "-" + (a.getMonth() + 1) + "-" + Math.min(a.getDate(), new Date(y, a.getMonth() + 1, 0).getDate())
        } else if (this.mode == "month") {
            let m = this.month + dir, y = this.year
            if (m < 1) { m = 12; y-- } else if (m > 12) { m = 1; y++ }
            this.navMonth = m; this.navYear = y
            this.navKey = y + "-" + m + "-" + Math.min(a.getDate(), new Date(y, m, 0).getDate())
        } else {
            const n = new Date(a.getFullYear(), a.getMonth(), a.getDate() + dir * (this.mode == "week" ? 7 : 1))
            this.navKey = this.root.keyOf(n); this.navYear = n.getFullYear(); this.navMonth = n.getMonth() + 1
            }
        },
    selectEvent(id: number, key: string?) {
        this.selectedId = id; this.openSection = 0
        if (key != null) this.navKey = key
        },
    closeDetail() { this.selectedId = -1 },

    /* ## Drag to reschedule
       Pointer capture, plus the runtime's click rule, give click-vs-drag for
       free: a gesture that moved is a drag and clicks nothing, so the block's
       `onClick` fires only on a real tap. The threshold below is the app's own
       (when the GHOST appears), not a click suppressor. A drop writes through
       the dataset's mutation API, so it wakes the derived model exactly like a
       title edit — no copy to rebuild. */

    startDrag(id: number, title: string, cat: string, timeLabel: string, w: number, h: number, gx: number, gy: number) {
        this.dragId = id; this.dragTitle = title; this.dragCat = cat; this.dragTimeLabel = timeLabel
        this.dragW = w; this.dragH = h; this.grabDX = gx; this.grabDY = gy
        this.dragging = false; this.dropKey = ""; this.downX = this.pointerX; this.downY = this.pointerY
        },
    dragMove() {
        if (this.dragId < 0) return
        if (!this.dragging) {
            const dx = this.pointerX - this.downX, dy = this.pointerY - this.downY
            if (dx * dx + dy * dy > 16) this.dragging = true
            }
        if (this.dragging) { const cell = this.cellAt(this.pointerX, this.pointerY); this.dropKey = cell != null ? cell.key : "" }
        },
    armDrag() {
        // The chip's hold fired: lift the ghost NOW, before any movement — on
        // touch this is the moment the claim engages, and the pickup should be
        // visible while the finger is still parked.
        if (this.dragId < 0) return
        this.dragging = true
        const cell = this.cellAt(this.pointerX, this.pointerY); this.dropKey = cell != null ? cell.key : ""
        },
    dropDrag(px: number, py: number, canceled: boolean) {
        if (this.dragId < 0) return
        // A drag never clicks — the runtime's own rule (a gesture whose pointer
        // wandered past slop resolves to no click), so the drop just commits —
        // but never an INTERRUPTED one: on touch the browser may take the
        // gesture for a scroll (a quick swipe over a chip), and that release
        // must not move the event to wherever the finger happened to be.
        if (this.dragging && !canceled) this.commitDrop(px, py)
        this.dragId = -1; this.dragging = false; this.dropKey = ""
        },
    cellAt(px: number, py: number) -> object {                         // invert the span mapping: screen point → grid cell
        const col = Math.floor((px - this.pad - this.gutter) / this.colW + this.c0)
        const row = Math.floor((py - this.barH - this.headH) / this.rowH + this.r0)
        return this.cal.value.grid[this.root.clamp(row, 0, this.monthRows - 1) * 7 + this.root.clamp(col, 0, 6)]
        },
    commitDrop(px: number, py: number) {
        const events = this.root.data.value != null ? this.root.data.value.events : []
        const idx = events.findIndex(e => e.id == this.dragId)
        if (idx < 0) return
        const ev = events[idx], p = ["events", idx]
        const cell = this.cellAt(px, py)
        if (cell != null) { const d = this.root.parseKey(cell.key); this.root.data.set([...p, "y"], d.getFullYear()); this.root.data.set([...p, "m"], d.getMonth() + 1); this.root.data.set([...p, "d"], d.getDate()) }
        if (this.blockness > 0.5) {          // a time view: also reschedule from the drop height
            const dur = ev.end - ev.start
            let s = Math.round(((py - this.barH - this.headH - this.grabDY) / this.rowH * 1440) / 15) * 15
            s = this.root.clamp(s, 0, 1440 - dur); this.root.data.set([...p, "start"], s); this.root.data.set([...p, "end"], s + dur)
            }
        },

    onInit() {
        if (this.root.env.base == null) this.data.fetch()      // hosted: auto refetches when env.base lands
        },

    /* ## Keyboard
       Arrows page the current view; Escape closes the detail panel. A Keys
       member — lifetime-managed, no listener to clean up. The arrows
       gate on the panel being CLOSED: its text fields own the keyboard while
       an event is being edited (Keys is the raw stream). */

    keys: Keys [
        onKeyUp(e: KeyEvent) {
            if (e.key == "Escape") this.root.closeDetail()
            else if (this.root.selectedId < 0 && e.key == "ArrowLeft") this.root.step(-1)
            else if (this.root.selectedId < 0 && e.key == "ArrowRight") this.root.step(1)
            }
        ],

    /* ## The surface — day / week / month → year
       For year the surface does not scale into its slot; each Cell re-lays-out into
       the current month's slot (driven by `app.yearZoom`), so the month becomes its mini. The
       other eleven months are the deferred `yearCal`. */

    board: View [ x = 0, y = { this.root.barH }, width = { this.root.bodyW }, height = { this.root.bodyH }, clip = true,

        // the month's backdrop: authored at the destination slot and scaled up about
        // its centre, so it starts full-bleed and converges by a pure scale to the mini

        monthBg: View [ x = { this.root.slotX }, y = { this.root.slotY }, width = { this.root.miniW }, height = { this.root.miniH },
            cornerRadius = 12, fill = { this.root.mix(this.theme.bg, this.theme.miniCurrentBg, this.root.yearZoom) },
            scale = { this.root.yearScale }, pivotX = { this.root.miniW / 2 }, pivotY = { this.root.miniH / 2 } ],
        weekdays: View [ opacity = { (1 - this.root.blockness) * (1 - this.root.yearZoom) }, datapath = { this.root.cal.value },
            View [ datapath = :cols[], key = :col, x = { this.root.pad + this.$data(["col"]) * (this.root.bodyW - 2 * this.root.pad) / 7 + 11 },
                l: Text [ y = 9, fontSize = 11, wrap = false, textColor = { this.theme.textMuted }, text = { this.$data(["name"]) } ]
                ]
            ],
        hours: View [ opacity = { this.root.blockness }, datapath = { this.root.cal.value },
            View [ datapath = :hours[], key = :h, y = { this.root.headH + this.$data(["h"]) / 24 * (this.root.bodyH - this.root.headH) }, width = { this.root.bodyW }, height = 1, fill = { this.theme.gridLine },
                lbl: Text [ x = 6, y = 1, fontSize = 10, wrap = false, textColor = { this.theme.hourLabel }, text = { this.$data(["label"]) } ]
                ]
            ],
        grid: View [ datapath = { this.root.cal.value },
            Cell [ datapath = :grid[], key = :key ]
            ],
        yearName: Text [ x = { this.root.slotX + 14 }, y = { this.root.slotY + 11 }, fontSize = 13, fontWeight = semibold, wrap = false,
            textColor = { this.theme.todayText }, text = { this.root.monthName(this.root.month) },
            opacity = { this.root.clamp((this.root.yearZoom - 0.5) / 0.5, 0, 1) } ]
        ],

    /* ## Year — the same surface pulled back to the full 4×3 grid, the eleven other
       months sweeping in around the shrinking board. */

    yearView: View [ y = { this.root.barH }, width = { this.root.bodyW }, height = { this.root.bodyH }, clip = true, visible = { this.root.yearZoom > 0.02 },
        opacity = { this.root.clamp((this.root.yearZoom - 0.5) / 0.3, 0, 1) },
        scale = { this.root.yearScale }, pivotX = { this.root.slotX + this.root.miniW / 2 }, pivotY = { this.root.slotY + this.root.miniH / 2 },
        grid: View [ width = { parent.width }, height = { parent.height }, datapath = { this.root.yearCal.value },
            MiniMonth [ datapath = :months[], key = :m ]
            ]
        ],

    /* ## Event detail panel
       Points its datapath at the selected event, so every field two-way binds
       straight to the record and reseeds when a different event opens. */

    panel: View [ width = { this.root.panelW }, height = { this.root.bodyH }, y = { this.root.barH }, fill = { this.theme.surface }, x = { this.root.width - this.root.panelInset },
        datapath = { this.root.data.value != null ? this.root.data.value.events.find(e => e.id == this.root.selectedId) : null },
        edge: View [ width = 1, height = { parent.height }, fill = { this.theme.line } ],
        secs: View [ x = 22, y = 24, width = { parent.width - 44 },
            layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 8 ],

            /* The EVENT section — the title block in the sections' own grammar: the
               same card, its label row carrying the panel's close where the others
               carry their chevron, the category color as the card's left edge, and
               the read-only date · time under the editable title. */

            ev: View [ width = { parent.width }, height = 112, cornerRadius = 10, clip = true, fill = { this.theme.sectionBg },
                rail: View [ width = 4, height = { parent.height }, fill = { this.root.catText(this.$data(["category"])) } ],
                hdr: View [ width = { parent.width }, height = 40,
                    lbl: Text [ x = 15, y = 16, fontSize = 12, fontWeight = bold, wrap = false, letterSpacing = 1,
                        textColor = { this.theme.textMuted }, text = "EVENT" ],
                    close: CloseIcon [ x = { parent.width - 28 }, y = 12, iconSize = 15,
                        ink = { this.theme.textMuted },
                        onClick() { this.root.closeDetail() }
                        ]
                    ],
                title: TextInput [ x = 13, y = 40, width = { parent.width - 26 }, height = 32, fontSize = 16, fontWeight = bold,
                    textColor = { this.theme.text }, placeholder = "Untitled event",
                    fill = { this.theme.fieldBg },
                    stroke = { stroke(1, this.focused ? this.theme.accent : this.theme.fieldEdge) },
                    text <-> :title ],
                meta: Text [ x = 15, y = 84, fontSize = 12.5, wrap = false, textColor = { this.theme.textMuted },
                    text = { this.root.dayLabel(this.$data(["y"]) + "-" + this.$data(["m"]) + "-" + this.$data(["d"])) + "  ·  " + this.root.shortTime(this.$data(["start"])) + " – " + this.root.shortTime(this.$data(["end"])) } ]
                ],

            DetailSection [ idx = 0, label = "NOTES",     field = "notes" ],
            DetailSection [ idx = 1, label = "LOCATION",  field = "location" ],
            DetailSection [ idx = 2, label = "ATTENDEES", field = "attendees" ]
            ]
        ],

    // the grabbed event, following the pointer during a drag

    ghost: View [ visible = { this.root.dragging }, opacity = 0.9, x = { this.root.pointerX - this.root.grabDX }, y = { this.root.pointerY - this.root.grabDY },
        width = { this.root.dragW }, height = { Math.max(this.root.dragH, 34) }, cornerRadius = 6, clip = true, fill = { this.root.catFill(this.root.dragCat) },
        shadow = shadow(0, 6, 16, #00000088),
        rail: View [ width = 3, height = { parent.height }, fill = { this.root.catText(this.root.dragCat) } ],
        tm: Text [ x = 11, y = 4, fontSize = 10, fontWeight = bold, wrap = false, textColor = { this.root.catText(this.root.dragCat) }, text = { this.root.dragTimeLabel } ],
        ti: Text [ x = 11, y = 17, fontSize = 11, wrap = false, textColor = { this.root.catText(this.root.dragCat) }, text = { this.root.dragTitle } ]
        ],

    /* ## Chrome
       Declared last for the top z-order. Three zones: brand + theme switch hug the
       left, Today + the view tabs hug the right, and the date nav floats near the
       centre, clamped so it never rides into either side. */

    bar: View [ width = { this.root.width }, height = { this.root.barH }, fill = { this.theme.bg },
        rule: View [ y = { parent.height - 1 }, width = { parent.width }, height = 1, fill = { this.theme.line } ],

        // Row-1 items center in the FIRST 60px band — fixed, not barH-derived,
        // so the narrow tier's second row doesn't drag them downward.

        brand: View [ x = 20, y = 19, height = 22,
            layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 5 ],

            // the word "Declare" is the way home — navigate() resolves against the
            // DISTRO root, so this works on either host at any mount point

            Text [ fontSize = 18, fontWeight = semibold, letterSpacing = { -0.02 * this.fontSize }, wrap = false, textFill = { gradient("90deg", this.theme.accent, this.theme.accentSecondary) }, text = "Declare",
                onClick() { this.root.navigate("apps/homepage/homepage.declare") }
                ],
            Text [ fontSize = 18, fontWeight = semibold, letterSpacing = { -0.02 * this.fontSize }, wrap = false, textColor = { this.theme.text }, text = "Calendar",
                visible = { !this.root.brandCompact } ]
            ],

        // Light / System / Dark — the house control, with the house marks. The
        // three glyphs this used to type (☀︎ ◐ ☾) were three unrelated corners
        // of whatever font the platform had; drawn, they share one disc and one
        // stroke, and four apps stop each drawing their own.

        themeSwitch: Segmented [ x = 196, height = 34, width = 94, y = 13,
            visible = { this.root.showTheme },
            iconSize = 15,
            value = { this.root.themeMode },
            input(v: object) { this.root.themeMode = "" + v },
            choices = { [ ({ id: "light", icon: "SunIcon" }),
                          ({ id: "auto",  icon: "AutoIcon" }),
                          ({ id: "dark",  icon: "MoonIcon" }) ] }
            ],

        // the date block is a fixed width per view, so the arrows hold still while
        // paging and re-place only on a view change

        // Narrow: the nav takes the second row, centered, with the whole width
        // to itself. Wide: it floats near the center, clamped off both side
        // clusters — and the clamp can never invert (the max is floored at the
        // min, so a squeezed bar pins the nav left rather than flinging it
        // off-frame, the bug the 480 floor used to paint).

        nav: View [ height = 34, y = { this.root.barNarrow ? 56 : 13 }, width = { this.root.navW },
            x = { this.root.barNarrow
                ? (this.root.width - this.root.navW) / 2
                : this.root.clamp((this.root.width - this.root.navW) / 2,
                            this.root.showTheme ? 300 : 190,
                            Math.max(this.root.showTheme ? 300 : 190, this.root.width - this.root.tabsW - this.root.navW - 120)) },
            prev:  NavArrow [ x = 0, dir = -1 ],
            title: Text [ x = 42, width = { this.root.dateW }, textAlign = center, y = 7, fontSize = 16, wrap = false,
                fontWeight = semibold, textColor = { this.theme.text }, text = { this.root.periodLabel } ],
            next:  NavArrow [ x = { this.root.dateW + 48 }, dir = 1 ]
            ],

        today: TextButton [ y = 13, x = { this.root.width - this.root.tabsW - (this.root.barNarrow ? 88 : 100) }, label = "Today" ],

        // Day / Week / Month / Year. This was the corpus's best segmented control
        // and its most bespoke one: a hand-built track, a hand-sprung pill, and
        // four hand-placed tabs with no keyboard at all. The pill's good idea —
        // spring a normalised LANE so a resize snaps instead of skating — is now
        // the library's, so adopting `Segmented` loses nothing and gains tab
        // stops, arrow roving, and the shared look.
        //
        // The labels shorten to single letters when the bar narrows, which the
        // data carries: `choices` is a constraint like any other.

        tabs: Segmented [ height = 34, width = { this.root.tabsW }, y = 13,
            x = { this.root.width - this.root.tabsW - (this.root.barNarrow ? 12 : 20) },
            value = { this.root.mode },
            input(v: object) { this.root.goMode("" + v) },
            choices = { [ ({ id: "day",   label: this.root.tabsCompact ? "D" : "Day" }),
                          ({ id: "week",  label: this.root.tabsCompact ? "W" : "Week" }),
                          ({ id: "month", label: this.root.tabsCompact ? "M" : "Month" }),
                          ({ id: "year",  label: this.root.tabsCompact ? "Y" : "Year" }) ] }
            ]
        ]
    ,
    // the traveling focus indicator — provided with the component library

    FocusRing [ ],
]
